description:
A value of a concrete type that implements a protocol IS a member of that
protocol's type. Today it is not: a protocol type and its implementers are
disjoint opaques, so the relation the whole dispatch layer depends on holds only
by fallback.

## THE ORIGINAL SYMPTOM IS FIXED -- this is now a MODEL ticket

Everything this was filed to fix is green at main 417c5b0b5. Do not start from
the old symptom list; it described a 2026-06-25 world.

Its own stated Checks pass:

    fn main() do
      dbg(Enum.to_list(1..3))
      dbg(Enum.reduce(1..3, 0, fn (x, acc) -> x + acc end))
      dbg(Enum.count([1,2,3]))
    end
    => [1, 2, 3] / 6 / 3

    Enum.to_list/1(impl-target::Range | {int,int,int} | %{...}) => [int] | []
    Enum.reduce/3(impl-target::Range | ..., int, (a2_p0,a2_p1) -> a2_r#67closure[]) => int
    Enum.count/1([int]) => int

The receiver arrives as the concrete impl-target union, the element stays `int`,
the bridge return is `[int]`, and there are no `any`-typed reduce/reverse
activations in the census at all.

The delta-debugged N-lambda ladder that once failed non-monotonically
(ok/ok/F/F/F/ok/F/F/F/ok at N=1..10) is also gone -- N=3, 5 and 7 all produce
correct output on run. That was resolved by fz-f98.16 (empty-list ambiguity
scoped per position), fz-f98.17 (a variable-carrying callee is absence, not a
dynamic edge) and fz-f98.18 (an uninhabitable callee makes the call dead), none
of which touched the protocol type model. `enum_take_drop_split` is green on all
three lanes.

Required-work bullet 4 is also DONE: `module_impl_target_ty_with` calls
`declared_struct_value_ty` and only falls back to `vec![any]` when the target
publishes no declared field types.

## WHAT REMAINS: the model itself

Bullets 1-3 are unbuilt, and they are the whole ticket now.

1. `resolve.rs` (`NominalKind::Opaque`) mints a protocol domain as
   `opaque_of(tag)` and DISCARDS the resolved params, so `Enumerable.t(a)`
   carries no `a`. It is disjoint from every impl target, so
   `intersect(Enumerable.t, Range)` is empty.
2. Because they are disjoint, a concrete receiver flowing into an
   `Enumerable.t` parameter survives only via `refine_contract_inputs`'
   empty-intersection FALLBACK -- it is never RELATED to the protocol type, and
   `a` is never bound.
3. `protocol_receiver_target_overlaps` still requires a non-empty intersect, so
   an opaque receiver finds no arm.

Model it as a BOUND its impls satisfy, carrying the parameter: impl-target types
become members, `intersect(impl, Protocol.t)` is the impl, and matching a
concrete receiver against `Protocol.t(a)` BINDS `a` to the receiver's element.
Then dispatch overlap and contract narrowing work by construction rather than by
empty-fallback.

## Evidence that this is a type-model problem, not a widening rule

fz-06a tried the widening approach at the dispatch layer and recorded the
boundary: envelope only the input ordinals some test actually reads. That fixed
the untested-SLOT half. Extending the same reasoning to variables NESTED beneath
a tested subject -- preserve the element of a tested list, the field of a tested
tuple -- costs 15 lib failures, because nested variables are load-bearing for the
reachability DECISION, not merely carried.

Read that falsified experiment before starting. It is direct evidence that the
remaining collapse needs the variable to become RESOLVABLE, not merely
un-widened -- which is what binding `a` at the protocol boundary would do.

## Not the problem

Not a bridge patch, not a convergence tweak, not an operator fix. The
provider-boundary `any` (`function_is_provider_boundary`) is the only LEGITIMATE
earned `any` and is unaffected.

## Checks

- `intersect(impl_target, Protocol.t)` is the impl target, not empty, for every
  registered impl.
- Matching a concrete receiver against `Protocol.t(a)` binds `a` to the
  receiver's element, verifiable in the activations dump without the
  empty-intersection fallback firing.
- `refine_contract_inputs`' empty-intersection fallback becomes unreachable for
  protocol-typed parameters (or is deleted).
- fz-f98.9's graduated-`any` count drops.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better; no protocol behavior regressions.

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-f98.11 P2 Values graduate to any before reaching Kernel arithmetic operators
- ◐ fz-f98.9 P1 Warn when a parameter or struct field type is graduated/defaulted to any (not declared any)
title: Protocol domain t(a) is a bare disjoint opaque that drops its parameter; impls are not members of it
